messages.subject: Choosing best K
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yuchao,

Thanks for the very nice tool!
When you use the BIC to select the most appropriate number of subclones (K), you seem to pick the model that gives the maximum BIC (based on you example codes).
However, with standard BIC formulation, the larger the BIC the lower the likelihood of the model. Therefore, we would traditionally pick the model with lowest BIC, right?
Could you please clarify this discrepancy?

Thanks!
Vitor

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Choosing best K
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vitor,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. We use BIC = 2 ln(L) − k ln(n), where L is the model likelihood, k is the number of parameters and n is the number of data points. The version you referred to (same as shown on the Wikipedia page of BIC https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayesian_information_criterion ) is what we defined with a negative sign. Both versions have been used and we adopt the former and thus pick the K that maximizes BIC.

Thanks for pointing this out. I will make sure to mark this and hope that this clarifies!

Yuchao

messages.subject: RE: Canopy - bootstrapping
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stefanie,

I’m not familiar with the newick format but the tree in Canopy is coded as a list embedded with tree elements and is plotted using R package ape. I am not sure why you want to use bootstrap on the tree, but if you want to get the confidence intervals or standard errors, since we are using the MCMC sampling procedure, you can get these by looking at the posterior distribution after binning and thinning. If you still want bootstrap, you will most likely have to code yourself from the tree, which again, is a list object in R.

Hope that this clarifies! I am cc’ing our mailing list in case other users have similar questions.

Best,

Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: Canopy - bootstrapping
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stephanie,

The trees from MCMC sampling after burnin and thinning are stored in a list with name samptreethin. You can get each posterior tree from this list. Each tree has its elements which are specified in our vignettes. You can get the standard errors from the posteriors of the tree elements.

Hope that this helps you and please feel free to let me know if you have further questions.

Best,
Yuchao

messages.subject: Pre-clustering step in Canopy
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yuchao,

I noticed that in your paper you use a pre-clustering step on the somatic mutations in cases when many mutations are present.
Is that functionality implemented as part of Canopy, or do you suggest using a different tool (e.g. SciClone) for clustering mutations, followed by application of Canopy?

Thanks!
Vitor
